mini_shai_hulud_apr_2026.title: Mini Shai-Hulud: SAP CAP framework worm (TeamPCP Wave 6)
mini_shai_hulud_apr_2026.family: self-propagating worm + credential stealer + CI abuse
mini_shai_hulud_apr_2026.notes: TeamPCP Wave 6. Cascading from Bitwarden CLI compromise (Wave 5). Preinstall hook downloads Bun 1.3.13, executes 11.7MB obfuscated JS (PBKDF2+SHA256 cipher, salt 'ctf-scramble-v2'). Steals credentials from 39+ file paths (GitHub, npm, AWS, Azure, GCP, SSH, Kubernetes, Terraform, crypto wallets, FileZilla). Exfiltrates via victim's own GitHub account (creates public repos with description 'A Mini Shai-Hulud has Appeared'). Injects Claude Code SessionStart hooks and VS Code folderOpen tasks for persistence. Installs self-hosted GHA runner named 'SHA1HULUD' with discussion.yaml C2 workflow. SAP CI abused via OIDC token exchange to publish @cap-js packages.

tanstack_shai_hulud_may_2026.title: Mini Shai-Hulud: TanStack Router Worm (TeamPCP Wave 7)
tanstack_shai_hulud_may_2026.family: self-propagating worm + credential stealer + provenance forging
tanstack_shai_hulud_may_2026.notes: CVE-2026-45321 (CVSS 9.6). CI pipeline hijack via pull_request_target + cache poisoning + OIDC memory extraction from runner /proc/pid/mem. 42 TanStack packages, 84 versions in 6-minute window. Payload: 2.3MB obfuscated router_init.js with beautify() AES decryption. Steals AWS, GCP, K8s, Vault, npm, GitHub, SSH, AI configs, browser passwords, crypto wallets. Exfiltrates via Session P2P (getsession.org). Self-propagates by republishing victim npm packages with forged Sigstore/SLSA provenance. Dead-man wiper: find ~ -type f -writable | xargs shred.

tanstack_secondary_victims_may_2026.title: Mini Shai-Hulud: Secondary Victims (Worm Propagation from TanStack)

mini_shai_hulud_tanstack_may_2026.notes: Self-spreading worm published 84 @tanstack/* versions across 42 packages plus 200+ versions across @mistralai, @opensearch-project, @uipath, @squawk, @draftlab, @draftauth, @tallyui, @beproduct, @ml-toolkit-ts, @taskflow-corp, @supersurkhet, @tolka, @cap-js, @dirigible-ai, @mesadev, and standalone pkgs. mini_shai_hulud_antv_atool_may_2026.title: MINI SHAI-HULUD AntV/atool wave
mini_shai_hulud_antv_atool_may_2026.notes: Compromised npm account "atool" was used to publish 643 malicious versions across 323 packages on 2026-05-19. Vendor reports describe the timing slightly differently: SafeDep observed two automated waves at 01:39-01:56 UTC and 02:05-02:06 UTC; Socket and StepSecurity describe a single 22-minute burst beginning ~01:56 UTC and continuing through ~02:56 UTC. Heaviest impact on the @antv/* ecosystem (~177 scoped packages); also hit the @openclaw-cn, @starmind, and @lint-md namespaces plus high-traffic standalone libs size-sensor (4.2M dl/mo), echarts-for-react (3.8M dl/mo), @antv/scale (2.2M dl/mo), timeago.js (1.15M dl/mo), and canvas-nest.js. Aggregate impact ~16M weekly downloads. Payload runs via preinstall hook ("bun run index.js") delivering a 498KB single-line obfuscated Bun bundle; one observed file SHA256 is a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c. Steals 20+ credential types (GitHub/CI tokens, AWS keys, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes service accounts, Vault tokens, SSH keys, Docker creds, DB connection strings) and attempts Docker container escape via the host socket. Primary exfil: HTTPS POST to t.m-kosche.com:443/api/public/otel/v1/traces with AES-256-GCM payload encryption + RSA-OAEP key wrapping. Fallback exfil: stolen GitHub token used to create a public repo under the victim's account named {dune-word}-{dune-word}-{0-999} (Dune-universe terminology; e.g. sayyadina-stillsuit-852) and commit stolen data into results/results-<timestamp>-<counter>.json. Beacon string left on every exfil repo's description and README: "niagA oG eW ereH :duluH-iahS" (character-reversed "Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again"). Persistence: .claude/settings.json SessionStart hooks, .vscode/tasks.json folderOpen tasks, kitty-monitor systemd/LaunchAgent units running ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py. Imposter commits planted in antvis/G2 forged to appear as huiyu.zjt <huiyu.zjt@ant.com> (a real maintainer). Some vendors attribute to TeamPCP (same actor as the May 12 TanStack wave); Socket and StepSecurity have not asserted attribution. Sources: - https://socket.dev/blog/antv-packages-compromised - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-antv-ecosystem - https://safedep.io/mini-shai-hulud-strikes-again-314-npm-packages-compromised/ - https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack - https://www.ox.security/blog/the-antv-ecosystem-was-compromised-with-shai-hulud-malware-300-packages-affected - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/mini-shai-hulud-pushes-malicious-antv.html

megalodon_tiledesk_may_2026.notes: Primary attack vector is GitHub-repo-side (5,561 repos backdoored via stolen PATs/deploy keys, malicious .github/workflows/ci.yml or docker-community-worker -push-latest.yml exfiltrating CI secrets to 216.126.225.129:8443). web3_defi_mcp_typosquats_may_2026.notes: Packages masquerade as legitimate Web3/DeFi developer security tools (MCP servers) while silently exfiltrating credentials, wallet keys, shell history, SSH keys, and environment variables on install and on every MCP tool invocation. polymarket_wallet_drainer_may_2026.notes: Nine npm packages impersonating legitimate Polymarket trading tools, all published by the attacker-controlled `polymarketdev` account. sl4x0_dependency_confusion_2025_2026.title: sl4x0 dependency-confusion campaign
sl4x0_dependency_confusion_2025_2026.notes: Sustained dependency confusion operation targeting Fortune 500 internal package names. 92+ packages published across 32 throwaway accounts (all under the *@sl4x0.xyz email domain; account-name convention is `<target>poc`). Payload is minimal: postinstall hook reads OS username + hostname + cwd basename + unix timestamp and exfiltrates them via DNS query to oob.sl4x0.xyz. No file or env theft, no persistence. Likely security research / bug bounty given the explicit "poc" naming, but it still executes on install and leaks developer identity to a third party. Only the 22 versions confirmed still live on npm as of 2026-03-24 are enumerated here; the 70+ removed packages are caught by the publisher fingerprint check (`@sl4x0.xyz` in `_npmUser` metadata). Source: https://safedep.io/sl4x0-dependency-confusion-campaign/

art_template_unc6691_may_2026.notes: Compromised maintainer account (npm: daughtrymom; GitHub: goofychris, renamed from `aui` in late November 2024) injected a stage-1 loader into the package's browser bundle (lib/template-web.js). durabletask_pypi_stealer_may_2026.title: durabletask PyPI multi-cloud credential stealer

laravel_lang_composer_may_2026.notes: An attacker with push access force-rewrote 700+ git tags across four community Composer packages (laravel-lang/lang ~502 tags, /http-statuses, /attributes, /actions) so EVERY version resolves to a malicious commit; RCE fires on Composer autoload (src/helpers.php added to autoload.files). miasma_redhat_cloud_services_wave_jun_20.title: MIASMA: @redhat-cloud-services npm scope compromise
miasma_redhat_cloud_services_wave_jun_20.notes: Compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account injected malicious code into 31 packages under the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope via orphan commits bypassing code review. Malicious GitHub Actions workflow triggered on branch push, requesting OIDC token with id-token:write to publish backdoored versions with valid SLSA provenance attestations. Payload: 4.2MB obfuscated index.js executed via preinstall hook, using ROT-21 + AES-128-GCM + obfuscator.io + B5 cipher (PBKDF2 200k iterations). Multi-stage credential harvester targeting GitHub/CI tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure creds, Kubernetes, Vault, npm/PyPI tokens, SSH keys, Docker, GPG. Process memory extraction reads /proc/<pid>/mem targeting Runner.Worker to steal live GitHub Actions secrets. Exfiltration via GitHub Contents API dead-drop (base64-encoded data in victim repos). Persistence via .claude/settings.json SessionStart hooks and .vscode/tasks.json folderOpen tasks. Self-propagating worm: uses harvested npm tokens with bypass_2fa to republish backdoored packages autonomously. Published via GitHub Actions OIDC from RedHatInsights/javascript-clients. ~80,000 aggregate weekly downloads. Wiz Research names this campaign "Miasma: The Spreading Blight". Two waves: 10:53 UTC and 13:44-13:46 UTC on June 1, 2026. Sources: https://www.wiz.io/blog/miasma-supply-chain-attack-targeting-redhat-npm-packages https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/multiple-redhat-cloud-services-npm-packages-compromised https://github.com/RedHatInsights/javascript-clients/issues/492

miasma_phantom_gyp_jun_2026.title: MIASMA: Phantom Gyp self-spreading worm wave
miasma_phantom_gyp_jun_2026.notes: Two days after the June 1 Miasma @redhat-cloud-services compromise, the same "Miasma: The Spreading Blight" campaign published 286 malicious versions across 57 packages in a rolling 2-hour burst. First victim: @vapi-ai/server-sdk (408K dl/mo) at 23:30 UTC; within an hour, ~50 packages in the jagreehal ecosystem (autotel-*, awaitly-*, executable-stories-*, node-env-resolver-*) plus ai-sdk-ollama (120K dl/mo) were republished by the compromised maintainer accounts. Cross-ecosystem: also injects into RubyGems via extconf.rb. Novel delivery ("Phantom Gyp"): a 157-byte binding.gyp file with command-substitution syntax <!(node index.js > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo stub.c) triggers code execution during `npm install`'s node-gyp rebuild step WITHOUT declaring any preinstall/postinstall script in package.json  -  bypassing every install-script monitor that only watches the package.json scripts block. This is the first observed in-the-wild abuse of binding.gyp for supply-chain execution. Payload hashes (SHA-256): ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90 (binding.gyp, 157 B) 5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61 (index.js root loader, 4.5 MB) da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707 (decrypted main, 668 KB) Obfuscation stack: ROT-9..ROT-20 Caesar + eval, AES-128-GCM self- decrypting blobs with embedded keys/IVs, a 907-byte Bun runtime loader that fetches bun-v1.3.13 from oven-sh/bun releases, and obfuscator.io wrapping a 2,306-entry encrypted string table on the main payload. Credential targets (20+ types): GitHub PATs and Actions secrets via /proc/<pid>/mem reads of Runner.Worker, AWS (env + IMDSv2 + ECS), GCP (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, service account keys), Azure (managed identity / IMDS), Kubernetes service accounts, HashiCorp Vault tokens, CircleCI, npm tokens, SSH keys, Docker socket creds (with host-socket container-escape attempt), 1Password, gopass, pass, and DB connection strings. Self-propagation: validates each stolen npm token against the keyword "IfYouInvalidateThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwner", enumerates the victim's packages, injects the binding.gyp + index.js payload into fresh tarballs, and republishes  -  with Sigstore provenance forgery in CI environments. C2 beacon for channel checks: GitHub commit search for "thebeautifulmarchoftime" (unauthenticated). User-Agent spoofed as python-requests/2.31.0 despite Bun runtime execution. Persistence (AI-assistant + editor poisoning via stolen GitHub tokens): .claude/setup.mjs, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen, .github/setup.js workflow injector. Exfiltration: HTTPS POST to GitHub Contents API repos/liuende501/{repo}/contents/results/results-{timestamp}.json with RSA-encrypted JSON envelopes; repos under github.com/liuende501 (236 at StepSecurity disclosure, 321+ at Snyk follow-up) named after Dune (atreides/fedaykin/sardaukar) and mythology (nemean/hydra/ cerberus/chimera) terms. 34 repo descriptions are tagged "Miasma - The Spreading Blight"; 195 carry the reversed beacon "niagA oG eW ereH :duluH-iahS". Sources: - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm - https://snyk.io/blog/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-self-propagating-npm-worm-binding-gyp/ - https://security.snyk.io/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-june-2026 - https://securityboulevard.com/2026/06/new-shai-hulud-miasma-wave-hits-hundreds-of-npm-packages/ - https://cybersecuritytimes.com/binding-gyp-attack/

miasma_hades_pypi_jun_2026.title: MIASMA "HADES": PyPI branch of the self-spreading worm
miasma_hades_pypi_jun_2026.notes: (37 PyPI wheels across 19 packages) Socket disclosed a single coordinated wave of 448 malicious artifacts (411 npm + 37 PyPI) from the same "Miasma: The Spreading Blight" campaign. The PyPI branch is tracked as "Hades - The End for the Damned". Novel PyPI delivery: each wheel ships a tiny "<name>-setup.pth" Python startup hook. Python auto-executes lines in a .pth file that begin with "import", so the hook execs an obfuscated _index.js loader at interpreter startup  -  triggering during plain `import`, with NO setup.py / build step and NO preinstall/postinstall hook to monitor. Payload hashes (SHA-256)  -  wired into MALICIOUS_HASHLIST: c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c (setup.pth hook, identical across all wheels) dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe (_index.js loader, 4.8 MB / 17 packages) e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d (_index.js loader variant, 4.7 MB / 2 packages) Credential targets (20+ types) and self-propagation mirror the June 1/3 npm Miasma waves. Dead-man's-switch token-nuke marker: "IfYouYankThisTokenItWillNukeTheComputerOfTheOwnerFully". C2 camouflage: exfiltrates over a path under the legitimate api.anthropic.com host (.../v1/api, which is NOT a real Anthropic endpoint). Exfil repos under github.com/<generated> use Greek-underworld names (stygian, tartarean, cerberus, charon, styx, lethe, thanatos, persephone); descriptions are tagged "Hades - The End for the Damned". Persistence via gh-token-monitor daemon, ~/.local/share/updater/update.py, .claude/setup.mjs, and a .github/workflows/codeql.yml workflow injector ("Run Copilot"). Sources: - https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-descends-to-hades-miasma-pypi-wave

ironworm_jun_2026.title: IRONWORM ("Shai-Hulud's rustier cousin") - 37 npm packages
ironworm_jun_2026.notes: A DISTINCT campaign from Miasma/Shai-Hulud (JFrog disclosure): a Rust-based infostealer pushed through 37 npm packages, all published by the npm account "asteroiddao" (operator "ocrybit"), spanning the weavedb / arnext / cwao / wdb Arweave-Web3 ecosystem. Delivery is a classic preinstall hook ("preinstall": "./tools/setup") that runs a ~976 KB Linux ELF stealer; it also rewrites existing GitHub Actions workflows for persistence and embeds an eBPF rootkit (q2.bpf.c) for process/network hiding. Targets crypto/Web3 developers: hooks the Exodus wallet Electron app (localhost:8738) to steal seed phrases, harvests 86+ env vars, 20+ credential files, AI/ML API keys, and Kubernetes/Vault secrets. C2 over Tor (/api/agent) with temp.sh as fallback exfil. Forged commit author "claude <claude@users.noreply.github.com>" across 57 backdated commits in 9 GitHub orgs. The operator leaked their own Ethereum address 0x7e28D9889f414B06c19a22A9Bd316f0AC279a4d6 (hardcoded BIP-39 seed in the exfil skip-list)  -  now flagged by the known-attacker-wallet check. Source: - https://research.jfrog.com/post/iron-worm-shai-hulud-rustier-cousin/

mastra_easy_day_js_jun_2026.title: MASTRA AI / "easy-day-js" - 141 @mastra packages + 2 deps
mastra_easy_day_js_jun_2026.notes: A DISTINCT campaign from Miasma/Shai-Hulud (Microsoft attribution: North Korea's Sapphire Sleet / BlueNoroff). In an 88-minute automated window (01:12-02:39 UTC) the attacker republished the entire @mastra/* npm scope plus the top-level mastra/create-mastra packages, each with a single injected dependency: easy-day-js, a typosquat of dayjs. easy-day-js@1.11.22 carries an obfuscated postinstall dropper (setup.cjs) that disables TLS verification (NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0), pulls a cross-platform infostealer from 23.254.164.92:8000/update/49890878 (stage-2 beacon to 23.254.164.123:443), and runs it as a detached hidden process. The stealer harvests host info, browser history, and 166 crypto-wallet browser extensions, then self-deletes. easy-day-js@1.11.21 is the clean "bait" version published for credibility. Content IoCs (C2 IPs, payload path, marker files) are flagged by check_easy_day_js_indicators. Sources: - https://research.jfrog.com/post/easy-day-js/ - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mastra-npm-packages-compromised-using-easy-day-js - https://orca.security/resources/blog/mastra-npm-supply-chain-attack/

miasma_leoplatform_rstreams_jun_2026.title: MIASMA "Mini Shai-Hulud" - LeoPlatform / RStreams (23 npm)
miasma_leoplatform_rstreams_jun_2026.notes: Socket disclosure: the Miasma/Phantom-Gyp self-spreading worm reaches the LeoPlatform and RStreams (AWS data-streaming) npm ecosystems, plus a handful of unrelated packages and one Go module (github.com/verana-labs/ verana-blockchain@v0.10.1-dev.20, not matchable here). Delivery is the now familiar binding.gyp install-time trigger plus editor/CI auto-run hooks (.claude/, .vscode/, .github/ setup scripts) that launch a Bun-bootstrapped _index.js payload. Payload/loader files are pinned by SHA-256 in MALICIOUS_HASHLIST; the campaign marker strings (RevokeAndItGoesKaboom, "Alright Lets See If This Works", thebeautifulmarchoftime) are matched by check_hades_miasma_indicators. Source: - https://socket.dev/blog/miasma-mini-shai-hulud-hits-leoplatform-npm-packages-go-ecosystem

shai_hulud_keyv_cacheable_aug_2026.title: SHAI-HULUD "Here We Go Again" - keyv / cacheable wave
shai_hulud_keyv_cacheable_aug_2026.notes: (443 npm packages, 2,235 versions; re-synced 2026-08-05, see block at end) The largest npm supply-chain wave to date by install volume: >2 billion monthly installs. Entry point was the compromised GitHub account of the keyv/cacheable maintainer. keyv@6.0.0 was published at 09:35 UTC; by 10:43 UTC the worm had republished eight further organizations at roughly one package per second each, driven by npm publish tokens harvested from the previous victim. Highest-volume packages: keyv (604M/mo), flat-cache (580M/mo), file-entry-cache (571M/mo), cacheable-request (137M/mo), cacheable (30M/mo). @or-sdk/auth and @arv-bedrock/auth-sso are authentication libraries, so downstream exposure compounds. Delivery: every poisoned release injects "preinstall": "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads Bun 1.3.13 from the genuine oven-sh GitHub release, runs a 727,680-byte Bun-compiled bundle (Math_Symbol.js / math_init.js, ten AES-256-GCM payloads keyed by PBKDF2, salt "svksjrhjkcejg", 200,000 iterations), then deletes the runtime. Infected repositories also receive .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook) and .vscode/tasks.json (runOn: folderOpen), both invoking setup.mjs  -  these are gated behind editor/agent workspace-trust prompts and only fire if the user accepts. Exfiltration uses NO attacker-controlled domain: harvested credentials are RSA-4096 encrypted and pushed to GitHub dead-drop repositories whose description contains "Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again" (~546-1,300 such repos created August 4). Persistence is a dead-man's switch installed as ~/.local/bin/gh-token-monitor.sh (macOS LaunchAgent com.user.gh-token-monitor / Linux systemd gh-token-monitor.service), polling GitHub every 60s and eval-ing an attacker-supplied handler when the stolen token is revoked  -  i.e. it fires on the standard incident-response action. Rotate credentials only from a host verified clean. NOTE: poisoned releases carry valid npm OIDC provenance and SLSA attestation, because the publishing CI itself was compromised. Provenance is NOT a safety signal for this wave. Content-based IoCs for this wave are covered by MALICIOUS_HASHLIST (setup.mjs x2, Math_Symbol.js), check_preinstall_bun_patterns ("node setup.mjs"), check_malicious_repo_descriptions ("Shai-Hulud: Here We Go Again") and the existing dead-man's-switch / AI-assistant-dropper checks. The per-version entries below come from the Wiz Research IoC CSV. Sources: - https://www.wiz.io/blog/keyv-and-cacheable-npm-supply-chain-attack (list: wiz-sec-public/wiz-research-iocs reports/keyv-packages.csv) - https://socket.dev/blog/popular-npm-packages-in-the-keyv-and-cacheable-namespaces-compromised-in-active-supply-chain - https://safedep.io/keyv-npm-supply-chain-compromise/ - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/keyv-and-friends-compromised-in-npm-supply-chain-attack

agentgate-agent-relay-npm-2026-09.title: Relay-driven AI-agent npm malware batch (AgentGate verification)
agentgate-agent-relay-npm-2026-09.family: relay-driven agent execution / config hijack / binary replacement / security-regression squatting
agentgate-agent-relay-npm-2026-09.notes: 18 packages tarball-verified malicious by AgentGate (2026-09-06) and re-verified by repo-forensics payload inspection (2026-09-09). Patterns: outbound WS/HTTPS relay driving local agent CLIs with permission bypass, OS autostart persistence, MCP/config hijack (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, mcp.json, SessionEnd hooks), credential-theft-via-agent-prompt, opencode binary replacement, and an MCP Inspector squat reverting the CVE-2025-49596 auth fix. Entire packages are malicious by design, so all versions are flagged.
